claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about P2Y2 structure shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: P2Y2 has been shown to interact with αV integrins through its RGD motif.
claims.source: P2Y2 has been shown to interact with αV integrins through this RGD motif (Erb et al., 2001), but the significance of this interaction has not been explored in cancer.
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Erb et al., 2001.

claims.claim: Immunofluorescence showed colocalization of integrin αV and P2Y2 in the PDAC cell lines AsPC-1, BxPC-3, and CAPAN-2.
claims.source: Immunofluorescence (IF) showed colocalization of integrin αV and P2Y2 in the PDAC cell lines AsPC-1 as well as PDAC cell lines with strong epithelial morphology, BxPC-3 and CAPAN-2, while MIA PaCa-2 cells showed low expression of both proteins, and PANC-1 showed high integrin αV and low P2Y2, matching CCLE data (Figure 2G; Figure 2—figure supplement 1F, G).
claims.evidence: Supported by IF imaging shown in Figure 2G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F, G.

claims.claim: MIA PaCa-2 cells showed low expression of both P2Y2 and integrin αV proteins.
claims.source: Immunofluorescence (IF) showed colocalization of integrin αV and P2Y2 in the PDAC cell lines AsPC-1 as well as PDAC cell lines with strong epithelial morphology, BxPC-3 and CAPAN-2, while MIA PaCa-2 cells showed low expression of both proteins, and PANC-1 showed high integrin αV and low P2Y2, matching CCLE data (Figure 2G; Figure 2—figure supplement 1F, G).
claims.evidence: Supported by IF imaging shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F, G.

claims.claim: PANC-1 cells showed high integrin αV and low P2Y2 expression.
claims.source: Immunofluorescence (IF) showed colocalization of integrin αV and P2Y2 in the PDAC cell lines AsPC-1 as well as PDAC cell lines with strong epithelial morphology, BxPC-3 and CAPAN-2, while MIA PaCa-2 cells showed low expression of both proteins, and PANC-1 showed high integrin αV and low P2Y2, matching CCLE data (Figure 2G; Figure 2—figure supplement 1F, G).
claims.evidence: Supported by IF imaging shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F, G.

claims.claim: Stellate cells are crucial for successful hanging drop sphere formation.
claims.source: PDAC cell lines were combined with stellate cells in a ratio of 1:2 (Kadaba et al., 2013), using an immortalized stellate cell line, PS-1 (Froeling et al., 2009) to form spheres (Figure 3A), recapitulating the ratios of the two biggest cellular components in PDAC. Stellate cells are crucial for successful hanging drop sphere formation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) and cancer cell invasion (Murray et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and citations to Kadaba et al., 2013; Froeling et al., 2009; Murray et al., 2022.

claims.claim: ATP (100 µM) increased invasion of AsPC-1 cells significantly compared to vehicle control (p<0.0001).
claims.source: Given that extracellular ATP concentration in tumors is in the hundred micromolar range (Pellegatti et al., 2008), spheres were treated with P2Y2 agonists ATP and UTP (100 µM). Both nucleotides increased invasion of the PDAC cell line AsPC-1 significantly compared to vehicle control (p<0.0001 and p=0.0013, respectively), and this was blocked by the P2Y2 selective antagonist AR-C (5 µM, p=0.0237, and p=0.0133; Figure 3B and C; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Supported by 3D spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3B, C and citation to Pellegatti et al., 2008.

claims.claim: UTP (100 µM) increased invasion of AsPC-1 cells significantly compared to vehicle control (p=0.0013).
claims.source: Given that extracellular ATP concentration in tumors is in the hundred micromolar range (Pellegatti et al., 2008), spheres were treated with P2Y2 agonists ATP and UTP (100 µM). Both nucleotides increased invasion of the PDAC cell line AsPC-1 significantly compared to vehicle control (p<0.0001 and p=0.0013, respectively), and this was blocked by the P2Y2 selective antagonist AR-C (5 µM, p=0.0237, and p=0.0133; Figure 3B and C; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Supported by 3D spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3B, C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: AR-C (5 µM) blocked ATP-driven invasion in AsPC-1 spheres (p=0.0237).
claims.source: Given that extracellular ATP concentration in tumors is in the hundred micromolar range (Pellegatti et al., 2008), spheres were treated with P2Y2 agonists ATP and UTP (100 µM). Both nucleotides increased invasion of the PDAC cell line AsPC-1 significantly compared to vehicle control (p<0.0001 and p=0.0013, respectively), and this was blocked by the P2Y2 selective antagonist AR-C (5 µM, p=0.0237, and p=0.0133; Figure 3B and C; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Supported by 3D spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3B, C.

claims.claim: AR-C (5 µM) blocked UTP-driven invasion in AsPC-1 spheres (p=0.0133).
claims.source: Given that extracellular ATP concentration in tumors is in the hundred micromolar range (Pellegatti et al., 2008), spheres were treated with P2Y2 agonists ATP and UTP (100 µM). Both nucleotides increased invasion of the PDAC cell line AsPC-1 significantly compared to vehicle control (p<0.0001 and p=0.0013, respectively), and this was blocked by the P2Y2 selective antagonist AR-C (5 µM, p=0.0237, and p=0.0133; Figure 3B and C; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Supported by 3D spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Treating spheres with AR-C on its own did not show significant effects on invasion.
claims.source: Treating spheres with AR-C on its own did not show significant effects on invasion (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Supported by 3D spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: A non-hydrolyzable ATP (ATPγS;100 µM) showed similar effects to ATP on invasion.
claims.source: Importantly, a non-hydrolyzable ATP (ATPγS;100 µM) showed similar effects to ATP, implicating ATP and not its metabolites as the cause of the invasion (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: Supported by 3D spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: PS-1 stellate cells showed negligible expression of P2Y2.
claims.source: Of note, IF staining of PS-1 cells showed negligible expression of P2Y2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: Supported by IF imaging shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: cRGDfV treatment reduced ATP-driven motility significantly in 3D spheroid invasion assays (p<0.0001).
claims.source: To determine whether integrin association was necessary for ATP-driven invasion, we treated spheres with 10 µM cyclic RGDfV peptide (cRGDfV), which binds predominantly to αVβ3 to block integrin binding to RGD motifs (Kapp et al., 2017), such as that in P2Y2 (Ibuka et al., 2015). cRGDfV treatment reduced ATP-driven motility significantly, both in 3D spheroid invasion assays (p<0.0001) (Figure 3B and C) and in 2D Incucyte migration assays (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, F) as did treatment with AR-C.
claims.evidence: Supported by 3D spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3B, C and citations to Kapp et al., 2017 and Ibuka et al., 2015.

claims.claim: cRGDfV binds predominantly to αVβ3 to block integrin binding to RGD motifs.
claims.source: To determine whether integrin association was necessary for ATP-driven invasion, we treated spheres with 10 µM cyclic RGDfV peptide (cRGDfV), which binds predominantly to αVβ3 to block integrin binding to RGD motifs (Kapp et al., 2017), such as that in P2Y2 (Ibuka et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Kapp et al., 2017 and Ibuka et al., 2015.

claims.claim: cRGDfV treatment reduced ATP-driven motility in 2D Incucyte migration assays.
claims.source: cRGDfV treatment reduced ATP-driven motility significantly, both in 3D spheroid invasion assays (p<0.0001) (Figure 3B and C) and in 2D Incucyte migration assays (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, F) as did treatment with AR-C.
claims.evidence: Supported by Incucyte migration assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, F.

claims.claim: BxPC-3 cells showed similar ATP-driven invasion behavior to AsPC-1 cells.
claims.source: To ensure that this behavior was not restricted to AsPC-1 cells, experiments were corroborated in the epithelial-like BxPC-3 cell line (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G, H; Tan et al., 1986).
claims.evidence: Supported by 3D spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G, H and citation to Tan et al., 1986.

claims.claim: Silencing P2Y2 expression in AsPC-1 cells using siRNA abrogated the invasive response to ATP (p<0.0001).
claims.source: To further verify that ATP-driven invasion was dependent on P2Y2, we silenced P2Y2 expression in AsPC-1 cells using siRNA (Figure 3D; Figure 3—figure supplement 1I), abrogating the invasive response to ATP (p<0.0001).
claims.evidence: Supported by 3D spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3D and siRNA validation shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1I.

claims.claim: AsPC-1 P2Y2CRISPR cells displayed a significant decrease in invasion compared to CTRCRISPR cells in both ATP-treated (p<0.0001) and non-treated (p=0.0005) conditions.
claims.source: P2Y2 involvement in this phenomenon was confirmed by generating a P2Y2 CRISPR-Cas9 AsPC-1 cell line (P2Y2CRISPR), which displayed a significant decrease in invasion compared to a control guide RNA CRISPR cell line (CTRCRISPR) in both ATP-treated (p<0.0001) and non-treated (p=0.0005) conditions (Figure 3F and E).
claims.evidence: Supported by 3D spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3E, F.

claims.claim: AR-C showed no significant off-target effects in AsPC-1 P2Y2CRISPR spheres.
claims.source: Additionally, we tested the off-target effects of AR-C in AsPC-1 P2Y2CRISPR spheres and confirmed no significant difference in invasion compared to the control (Figure 3—figure supplement 1J).
claims.evidence: Supported by 3D spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1J.

claims.claim: The RGD motif of P2Y2 is essential for ATP-driven cancer cell invasion.
claims.source: Together, these findings demonstrate that P2Y2 is essential for ATP-driven cancer cell invasion. To determine the importance of the RGD motif of P2Y2 in ATP-driven invasion, we obtained a mutant P2Y2 construct, where the RGD motif was replaced by RGE (P2Y2RGE), which has less affinity for αV integrins (Erb et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: Inferred from the collective experimental results with siRNA, CRISPR, and RGE mutant.

claims.claim: The P2Y2RGE mutant has less affinity for αV integrins than wild-type P2Y2.
claims.source: To determine the importance of the RGD motif of P2Y2 in ATP-driven invasion, we obtained a mutant P2Y2 construct, where the RGD motif was replaced by RGE (P2Y2RGE), which has less affinity for αV integrins (Erb et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Erb et al., 2001.

claims.claim: Only AsPC-1 P2Y2CRISPR spheres containing P2Y2RGD transfected cells demonstrated a rescue of the ATP-driven invasive phenotype (p<0.0001).
claims.source: This mutant was transfected into AsPC-1 P2Y2CRISPR cells and compared to cells transfected with wild-type P2Y2 (P2Y2RGD; Figure 3—figure supplement 1K). Only spheres containing P2Y2RGD transfected cells demonstrated a rescue of the ATP-driven invasive phenotype (p<0.0001; Figure 3G and H), with P2Y2RGE spheres not responding to ATP treatment.
claims.evidence: Supported by 3D spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3G, H.

claims.claim: P2Y2RGE spheres did not respond to ATP treatment.
claims.source: This mutant was transfected into AsPC-1 P2Y2CRISPR cells and compared to cells transfected with wild-type P2Y2 (P2Y2RGD; Figure 3—figure supplement 1K). Only spheres containing P2Y2RGD transfected cells demonstrated a rescue of the ATP-driven invasive phenotype (p<0.0001; Figure 3G and H), with P2Y2RGE spheres not responding to ATP treatment.
claims.evidence: Supported by 3D spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3G, H.

claims.claim: No ATP-driven invasion was observed in PANC-1 cells transfected with an empty vector or with P2Y2RGE.
claims.source: To ensure this behavior was not influenced by off-target CRISPR effects, we repeated the experiment in PANC-1 cell line, which expresses very low levels of P2Y2, but high levels of integrin αV (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F, G). No ATP-driven invasion was observed in PANC-1 cells transfected with an empty vector (EV) or with P2Y2RGE (Figure 3I and J).
claims.evidence: Supported by 3D spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3I, J.

claims.claim: Only PANC-1 cells transfected with P2Y2RGD showed ATP-driven invasion (p<0.0001).
claims.source: Only when transfecting PANC-1 cells with P2Y2RGD was ATP-driven invasion observed (p<0.0001).
claims.evidence: Supported by 3D spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3I, J.

claims.claim: The RGD motif of P2Y2 is required for ATP-driven cancer cell invasion.
claims.source: These results demonstrate that the RGD motif of P2Y2 is required for ATP-driven cancer cell invasion.
claims.evidence: Conclusion drawn from the collective experimental results with P2Y2RGD and P2Y2RGE mutants.

claims.claim: The density of P2Y2 proteins at the membrane decreased by 42% when P2Y2RGD cells were treated with ATP, compared to control (p<0.0001).
claims.source: We imaged AsPC-1 P2Y2CRISPR cells transfected with P2Y2RGD or P2Y2RGE in the absence or presence of 100 µM ATP for 1 hr (Figure 4D), observing a 42% decrease in the median density of P2Y2 proteins at the membrane when P2Y2RGD cells were treated with ATP, compared to control (p<0.0001; Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: Supported by DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 4D, E.

claims.claim: A slight decrease in the density of P2Y2 proteins on P2Y2RGE cells following ATP treatment was not statistically significant (p=0.1570).
claims.source: In contrast, although a slight decrease in the density of P2Y2 proteins on P2Y2RGE cells was observed following ATP treatment, this was not statistically significant (p=0.1570).
claims.evidence: Supported by DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: The density of P2Y2 proteins and protein clusters in both P2Y2RGD and P2Y2RGE controls were equivalent (p>0.9999).
claims.source: The density of P2Y2 proteins and protein clusters in both P2Y2RGD and P2Y2RGE controls were equivalent (Figure 4E and F; p>0.9999), indicating similar expression of the receptor at the surface in both control conditions.
claims.evidence: Supported by DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 4E, F.

claims.claim: The density of P2Y2 clusters decreased significantly in both P2Y2RGD and P2Y2RGE conditions when treated with ATP (43% decrease, p<0.0001 for P2Y2RGD, and 48% decrease, p=0.0002 for P2Y2RGE).
claims.source: Interestingly, the density of P2Y2 clusters decreased significantly in both conditions when treated with ATP (Figure 4F; 43% decrease, p<0.0001 for P2Y2RGD, and 48% decrease, p=0.0002 for P2Y2RGE).
claims.evidence: Supported by DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: ATP treatment of normal AsPC-1 cells resulted in a 68% decrease in P2Y2 at the membrane (p<0.0001), while co-treatment with cRGDfV prevented this change (p>0.9999).
claims.source: We repeated these studies with normal AsPC-1 cells (untransfected and with unaltered P2Y2 expression) treated with ATP +/-cRGDfV, only observing a reduction of P2Y2 at the membrane with ATP alone (68% decrease, p<0.0001), while co-treatment with cRGDfV prevented this change (p>0.9999; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
claims.evidence: Supported by DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B.

claims.claim: The RGD motif is required for αV integrin to control P2Y2 levels at the membrane.
claims.source: These findings highlight that the RGD motif is required for αV integrin to control P2Y2 levels at the membrane.
claims.evidence: Conclusion drawn from DNA-PAINT experiments with P2Y2RGD, P2Y2RGE, and cRGDfV treatments.

claims.claim: Stimulating P2Y2RGD with ATP increased the density of αV molecules and αV clusters at the membrane (p=0.0003).
claims.source: Turning to αV integrins, we observed an increase in the density of αV molecules and αV clusters at the membrane when stimulating P2Y2RGD with ATP (165 αV molecules/ROI, IQR = 162.75; 6.5 αV clusters/ROI, IQR = 8.75) compared to P2Y2RGD without stimulation (58 αV molecules/ROI, IQR = 41; 2.5 αV clusters/ROI, IQR = 2; p=0.0003; Figure 4G and H).
claims.evidence: Supported by DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 4G, H.

claims.claim: Normal AsPC-1 cells showed significantly more αV molecules and clusters following ATP stimulation (p=0.0382 and p=0.0349).
claims.source: This phenomenon was also observed with normal AsPC-1 cells, with significantly more αV molecules and clusters (p=0.0382 and p=0.0349) detected following ATP stimulation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, D).
claims.evidence: Supported by DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, D.

claims.claim: P2Y2RGE transfected cells exhibited more αV molecules and clusters at the membrane compared to P2Y2RGD cells in absence of stimulation (p=0.0003, p=0.0024, respectively).
claims.source: In absence of stimulation, P2Y2RGE transfected cells exhibited more αV molecules and clusters at the membrane (182 αV molecules/ROI, IQR = 262.75; 9 αV clusters/ROI IQR = 14) compared to P2Y2RGD cells (p=0.0003, p=0.0024, respectively).
claims.evidence: Supported by DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 4G, H.

claims.claim: Treating P2Y2RGE cells with ATP did not result in significant changes in αV molecules and clusters (p=0.7086; p=0.1846).
claims.source: However, treating P2Y2RGE cells with ATP did not result in significant changes in αV molecules and clusters (p=0.7086; p=0.1846).
claims.evidence: Supported by DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 4G, H.

claims.claim: The increase in the number of αV clusters was due to an increase in the number of αV proteins at the membrane.
claims.source: When the number of clusters was normalized with the number of αV molecules, to obtain the percentage of αV in clusters (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E), there was no significant difference between conditions (p>0.9999), indicating that the increase in the number of αV clusters was due to an increase in the number of αV proteins at the membrane.
claims.evidence: Supported by DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: Activated P2Y2 has an RGD motif-dependent function in localizing integrin αV to the membrane.
claims.source: Taken together, these data indicate an RGD motif-dependent function of activated P2Y2 in localizing integrin αV to the membrane.
claims.evidence: Conclusion drawn from DNA-PAINT experiments showing differential αV localization with P2Y2RGD vs P2Y2RGE.

claims.claim: A higher percentage of integrin αV proteins were in <50 nm proximity to P2Y2 in P2Y2RGD cells following ATP stimulation (103% increase, p=0.0143).
claims.source: We detected a higher percentage of integrin αV proteins in <50 nm proximity to P2Y2 in P2Y2RGD cells following ATP stimulation (Figure 4I; 103% increase, p=0.0143).
claims.evidence: Supported by nearest neighbor distance analysis from DNA-PAINT data shown in Figure 4I.

claims.claim: P2Y2RGE cells stimulated with ATP showed a 43% decrease (p=0.0101) in αV molecules in close proximity to P2Y2 in comparison to unstimulated cells.
claims.source: In contrast, P2Y2RGE cells stimulated with ATP showed a 43% decrease (p=0.0101) in αV molecules in close proximity to P2Y2 in comparison to unstimulated cells.
claims.evidence: Supported by nearest neighbor distance analysis from DNA-PAINT data shown in Figure 4I.

claims.claim: ATP-stimulated P2Y2RGD and unstimulated P2Y2RGE cells showed an increased percentage of αV proteins spaced at 20-100 nm range compared to untreated P2Y2RGD cells (98% increase with p=0.0132 and 89% increase with p=0.0181).
claims.source: Analyzing the percentage of αV proteins with NND in the 20–100 nm range, we saw a similar pattern (Figure 4J). ATP-stimulated P2Y2RGD and unstimulated P2Y2RGE cells showed an increased percentage of αV proteins spaced at this range compared to untreated P2Y2RGD cells (98% increase with p=0.0132 and 89% increase with p=0.0181).
claims.evidence: Supported by nearest neighbor distance analysis from DNA-PAINT data shown in Figure 4J.

claims.claim: No significant changes were observed in NND of <20 nm between αV proteins in any of the conditions.
claims.source: No significant changes were observed in NND of <20 nm between αV proteins in any of the conditions (Figure 4K).
claims.evidence: Supported by nearest neighbor distance analysis from DNA-PAINT data shown in Figure 4K.

claims.claim: P2Y2RGD molecules were in significantly closer proximity to each other compared to P2Y2RGE in control and stimulated conditions (p<0.0001 and p=0.007).
claims.source: In contrast, P2Y2RGD molecules were in significantly closer proximity to each other compared to P2Y2RGE in control and stimulated conditions (p<0.0001 and p=0.007) (Figure 4L).
claims.evidence: Supported by nearest neighbor distance analysis from DNA-PAINT data shown in Figure 4L.

claims.claim: There is a reciprocal interaction between αV integrin and P2Y2 receptors, where P2Y2 can alter integrin localization to the plasma membrane while αV integrins influence activated P2Y2 membrane localization.
claims.source: In summary, our SMLM studies demonstrate a reciprocal interaction between αV integrin and P2Y2 receptors, where P2Y2 can alter integrin localization to the plasma membrane while αV integrins influence activated P2Y2 membrane localization.
claims.evidence: Conclusion drawn from the collective DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy experiments.

claims.claim: AsPC-1 cells displayed a significant increase of FAK and ERK phosphorylation after 15 min of ATP stimulation, which was abrogated by concomitant targeting of P2Y2 with AR-C.
claims.source: There is growing evidence of the importance of endosomal GPCR signaling and its potential relevance in disease and therapeutic opportunities (Calebiro and Godbole, 2018). As we identified the RGD motif in P2Y2 having a possible role in receptor internalization, integrin dynamics, and invasion, we proceeded to look at integrin signaling through phosphorylation of FAK (p-FAK) and ERK (p-ERK) from 0 to 1 hr after treating with 100 µM ATP. AsPC-1 cells displayed a significant increase of FAK and ERK phosphorylation after 15 min of ATP stimulation, which was abrogated by concomitant targeting of P2Y2 with AR-C (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5A and citation to Calebiro and Godbole, 2018.

claims.claim: Impairing the RGD motif function in P2Y2 with cRGDfV or by transfecting AsPC-1 P2Y2CRISPR cells with the P2Y2RGE mutant decreased p-FAK and p-ERK levels.
claims.source: When impairing the RGD motif function in P2Y2 with cRGDfV or by transfecting AsPC-1 P2Y2CRISPR cells with the P2Y2RGE mutant, p-FAK, and p-ERK levels decreased (Figure 5B and C).
claims.evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5B, C.

claims.claim: Targeting the RGD motif in P2Y2 impairs receptor signaling and inhibits pancreatic cancer cell invasion.
claims.source: Collectively, targeting the RGD motif in P2Y2 impairs receptor signaling and inhibits pancreatic cancer cell invasion.
claims.evidence: Conclusion drawn from the collective experimental results showing effects of RGD motif targeting on signaling and invasion.

claims.claim: Purinergic signaling has been associated classically with hypoxia and immune function in cancer.
claims.source: Purinergic signaling has been associated classically with hypoxia and immune function in cancer (Di Virgilio et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Di Virgilio et al., 2018.

claims.claim: Hypoxia induces ATP release in cells, as first reported in rat heart cells.
claims.source: One of the first reports of hypoxia-inducing ATP release in cells identified an increase of extracellular ATP in rat heart cells when kept in hypoxic conditions (Forrester and Williams, 1977).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Forrester and Williams, 1977.

claims.claim: PDAC is a highly hypoxic cancer, with high levels of ATP reported in the tumor interstitial fluid of human and mouse PDAC tissues compared to healthy tissues.
claims.source: PDAC is a highly hypoxic cancer, with high levels of ATP reported in the tumor interstitial fluid of human and mouse PDAC tissues compared to healthy tissues (Hu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Hu et al., 2019.

claims.claim: Expression of most purinergic genes was associated predominantly with immune cells, immunogenic PDAC subtype, and low hypoxia scores.
claims.source: Expression of most purinergic genes was associated predominantly with immune cells, immunogenic PDAC subtype, and low hypoxia scores (Figure 1C and E).
claims.evidence: Supported by bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 1C, E.

claims.claim: Expression of genes correlated with worse survival and hypoxia (PANX1, NT5E, ADORA2B, and P2RY2) was associated with tumor cells and the squamous PDAC subtype.
claims.source: In contrast, expression of genes correlated with worse survival and hypoxia (PANX1, NT5E, ADORA2B, and P2RY2) was associated with tumor cells and the squamous PDAC subtype, correlating with hypoxia, inflammation, and worse prognosis (Bailey et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by bioinformatic analysis and citation to Bailey et al., 2016.

claims.claim: The squamous PDAC subtype correlates with hypoxia, inflammation, and worse prognosis.
claims.source: In contrast, expression of genes correlated with worse survival and hypoxia (PANX1, NT5E, ADORA2B, and P2RY2) was associated with tumor cells and the squamous PDAC subtype, correlating with hypoxia, inflammation, and worse prognosis (Bailey et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Bailey et al., 2016.

claims.claim: The adenosine A2B receptor requires larger agonist concentrations for activation compared to other receptors in the same family, such as adenosine A2A.
claims.source: Adenosine A2B receptor requires larger agonist concentrations for activation compared to other receptors in the same family, such as adenosine A2A (Bruns et al., 1986; Xing et al., 2016), and receptor expression has been reported to increase when cells are subjected to hypoxia (Feoktistov et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Bruns et al., 1986 and Xing et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Adenosine A2B receptor expression has been reported to increase when cells are subjected to hypoxia.
claims.source: Adenosine A2B receptor requires larger agonist concentrations for activation compared to other receptors in the same family, such as adenosine A2A (Bruns et al., 1986; Xing et al., 2016), and receptor expression has been reported to increase when cells are subjected to hypoxia (Feoktistov et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Feoktistov et al., 2004.

claims.claim: HIF-1α has been shown to upregulate A2B and P2Y2 expression in liver cancer.
claims.source: Moreover, HIF-1α has been shown to upregulate A2B and P2Y2 expression in liver cancer (Tak et al., 2016; Kwon et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Tak et al., 2016 and Kwon et al., 2019.

claims.claim: P2Y2 activation with ATP led to elevated HIF-1α expression in PDAC.
claims.source: These observations were supported by published immunohistochemical staining of 264 human PDAC samples, showing that P2Y2 localized predominantly in cancer cells in human PDAC and that P2Y2 activation with ATP led to elevated HIF-1α expression (Hu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Hu et al., 2019.

claims.claim: P2Y2 has been associated with cancer cell growth and glycolysis in PDAC.
claims.source: P2Y2 has been associated with cancer cell growth and glycolysis in PDAC (Ko et al., 2012; Hu et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Ko et al., 2012; Hu et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2020.

claims.claim: Combination treatment of subcutaneous xenografts of AsPC-1 or BxPC-3 cells with the P2Y2 antagonist AR-C together with gemcitabine significantly decreased tumor weight and resulted in increased survival compared to placebo or gemcitabine monotherapy control.
claims.source: Combination treatment of subcutaneous xenografts of AsPC-1 or BxPC-3 cells with the P2Y2 antagonist AR-C together with gemcitabine significantly decreased tumor weight and resulted in increased survival compared to placebo or gemcitabine monotherapy control (Hu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Hu et al., 2019.

claims.claim: Increased glycolysis and cytoskeletal rearrangements have been linked.
claims.source: Increased glycolysis and cytoskeletal rearrangements have been linked (Park et al., 2020), and both events could occur downstream of P2Y2 activation.
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Park et al., 2020.

claims.claim: P2Y2 has been implicated in invasive phenotypes in prostate, breast, and ovarian cancer.

claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Jin et al., 2014; Li et al., 2015; Martínez-Ramírez et al., 2016.

results.result: PDAC has poor survival outcomes with minimal improvement over 50 years. PDAC accounts for 90% of pancreatic cancer cases, has the lowest survival rate among solid malignancies, with >80% presenting with unresectable tumors, <5% five-year survival, and is predicted to become the second leading cause of cancer death by 2040, primarily due to chemoresistance.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C11-C18 collectively establish PDAC's poor prognosis through multiple cited sources (Kocher 2023, Bengtsson et al. 2020, Rahib et al. 2021, Neuzillet et al. 2017) and established epidemiological knowledge. The claims are internally consistent and well-supported by the literature.

results.result: PDAC is characterized by hypoxia and elevated extracellular ATP levels. The desmoplastic stroma causes impaired vascularization and hypoxia, leading to cellular stress and ATP release into the tumor microenvironment at concentrations 200-fold higher than normal tissue.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C19-C21, C103 are well-supported by multiple citations (Koong et al. 2000, Di Maggio 2016, Forrester and Williams 1977, Pellegatti et al. 2008, Hu et al. 2019). The mechanistic link between hypoxia, cellular stress, and ATP release is established, and the 200-fold elevation is specifically cited.

results.result: The purinergic signaling axis comprises druggable membrane proteins regulating ATP and adenosine, with distinct biological functions. ATP promotes inflammation, growth, and cell movement, while adenosine is anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive. Clinical trials targeting CD73 and adenosine receptor 2A are ongoing, though one Phase II study was withdrawn due to minimal activity.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C22-C29 are supported by multiple citations and clinical trial identifiers. The characterization of the purinergic axis, its components, and their biological functions are well-documented. The clinical trial information is verifiable through NCT identifiers.

results.result: P2RY2 is the purinergic gene most strongly associated with poor outcomes in PDAC. Bioinformatic analysis of TCGA data shows P2RY2 has the highest hazard ratio (2.99, p=8.5×10⁻⁵), strongest correlation with hypoxia scores (log2 ratio >0.5, FDR<0.0001), highest cancer cell-specific expression, and greatest adverse impact on patient survival among purinergic genes.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C6, C30, C36-C37, C41, C43-C44 are supported by comprehensive bioinformatic analyses shown in Figures 1B, 1C, 1D, 1E and supplementary figures. The statistical values are specific and the analyses use appropriate TCGA datasets (n=177). Multiple independent analytical approaches converge on P2RY2.

results.result: Purinergic genes show distinct expression patterns across PDAC molecular subtypes. Most purinergic genes associate with immunogenic subtypes and immune cells, while genes correlated with worse survival (PANX1, NT5E, ADORA2B, P2RY2) associate with tumor cells and the squamous subtype, which correlates with hypoxia and worse prognosis.
results.evaluation: Claims C31-C34, C104-C106 are supported by molecular subtyping analyses (Bailey, Collisson, Moffitt classifications) with appropriate citations and data shown in Supplementary file 1 and Figures 1C, 1E. The distinction between immune-associated and tumor-associated purinergic genes is well-documented.

results.result: Hypoxia-associated purinergic genes show tumor-specific expression patterns. Analysis of microdissected PDAC samples (n=60) shows P2RY2, ADORA2B, and NT5E are expressed in tumor epithelial tissue, while PANX1 (involved in ATP release) is expressed in stromal tissue. Hypoxia is associated with worse survival (p=0.002).
results.evaluation: Claims C35, C38-C40 are supported by differential expression analysis of GSE93326 data (Maurer et al. 2019) shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B. The tissue-specific localization is clearly demonstrated, and the survival association with hypoxia is statistically significant.

results.result: P2Y2 expression is elevated in PDAC tumors and predicts poor survival. RNAscope validation (n=3) confirmed P2Y2 mRNA localization to tumor epithelium. TCGA/GTEx analysis (n=179 tumor, n=171 normal) showed significantly higher P2Y2 in tumors (p<0.0001). High P2Y2 expression associated with decreased median survival (67.87 vs 17.27 months).
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C47 are supported by RNAscope data (Figure 2A), GEPIA analysis (Figure 2B), and Kaplan-Meier analysis (Figure 2C). The validation uses multiple independent approaches and appropriate sample sizes. The survival difference is substantial and statistically significant.

results.result: P2Y2 function in PDAC is linked to integrin signaling and cytoskeletal dynamics. GSEA of TCGA (n=177) and CPTAC (n=140) cohorts identified 'integrin signaling pathway' as the top enriched pathway. ATP (100 µM) induced cytoskeletal rearrangements in AsPC-1 cells, blocked by P2Y2 antagonist AR-C (5 µM), with dose-response validation.
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C52 are supported by GSEA analysis (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) and Incucyte live-cell imaging (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D-E). The functional validation with pharmacological inhibition and dose-response studies strengthens the bioinformatic predictions.

results.result: P2Y2 contains a unique RGD motif that mediates integrin interactions. P2Y2 is the only P2Y GPCR with an RGD motif in the first extracellular loop, shown to interact with αV integrins. Immunofluorescence confirmed colocalization in AsPC-1, BxPC-3, and CAPAN-2 cells, with variable expression patterns in MIA PaCa-2 and PANC-1 cells matching CCLE data.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C57 are supported by structural knowledge (Figure 2F), citation to Erb et al. 2001, and IF imaging (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1F-G). The expression patterns across cell lines are consistent with CCLE database, providing orthogonal validation.

results.result: P2Y2 is critical for ATP-driven invasion in 3D PDAC spheroid models. Using spheres with 1:2 cancer:stellate cell ratio, ATP and UTP (100 µM) significantly increased AsPC-1 invasion (p<0.0001, p=0.0013), blocked by AR-C (p=0.0237, p=0.0133). Non-hydrolyzable ATPγS showed similar effects, implicating ATP directly. PS-1 stellate cells showed negligible P2Y2 expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C58-C65 are supported by 3D spheroid invasion assays (Figure 3A-C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-D) with appropriate statistical analysis (n=3 biological replicates). The use of non-hydrolyzable ATP and verification of stellate cell P2Y2 expression strengthen the mechanistic interpretation. AR-C alone showed no effect, supporting specificity.

results.result: Blocking P2Y2-integrin interactions inhibits ATP-driven invasion. The cyclic RGDfV peptide (10 µM), which binds αVβ3 integrins, significantly reduced ATP-driven invasion in 3D spheroids (p<0.0001) and 2D migration assays. Similar effects were observed in BxPC-3 cells, confirming the behavior is not cell line-specific.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C69 are supported by invasion assays with cRGDfV treatment (Figure 3B-C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1E-H) and appropriate citations (Kapp et al. 2017, Ibuka et al. 2015, Tan et al. 1986). Testing in multiple cell lines and assay formats strengthens the conclusion.

results.result: P2Y2 is essential for ATP-driven invasion through genetic validation. siRNA knockdown of P2Y2 abrogated ATP-driven invasion (p<0.0001). CRISPR-Cas9 knockout (P2Y2CRISPR) showed decreased invasion in both ATP-treated (p<0.0001) and untreated (p=0.0005) conditions. AR-C showed no off-target effects in P2Y2CRISPR cells, confirming specificity.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C73 are supported by siRNA experiments (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1I) and CRISPR knockout studies (Figure 3E-F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1J). The use of both transient knockdown and stable knockout, plus off-target control experiments, provides strong genetic evidence for P2Y2's essential role.

results.result: The RGD motif of P2Y2 is required for ATP-driven invasion. P2Y2RGE mutant (reduced integrin affinity) failed to rescue invasion in P2Y2CRISPR cells, while P2Y2RGD restored the phenotype (p<0.0001). In PANC-1 cells (low endogenous P2Y2), only P2Y2RGD transfection enabled ATP-driven invasion (p<0.0001), not empty vector or P2Y2RGE.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C79 are supported by rescue experiments in P2Y2CRISPR cells (Figure 3G-H) and gain-of-function studies in PANC-1 cells (Figure 3I-J). The use of both loss-of-function rescue and gain-of-function approaches, with RGD vs RGE comparison, provides strong evidence for the RGD motif's requirement. The P2Y2RGE mutant serves as an excellent negative control.

results.result: The RGD motif regulates P2Y2 membrane localization upon ATP stimulation. DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy showed ATP treatment decreased P2Y2RGD membrane density by 42% (p<0.0001), but not P2Y2RGE (p=0.1570). P2Y2 cluster density decreased in both conditions. In normal AsPC-1 cells, ATP reduced P2Y2 by 68% (p<0.0001), prevented by cRGDfV co-treatment (p>0.9999).
results.evaluation: Claims C80-C85 are supported by quantitative DNA-PAINT analysis (Figure 4D-F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-B) with appropriate statistical analysis (n=21 ROIs from ≥5 cells per condition). The differential effects of P2Y2RGD vs P2Y2RGE and the cRGDfV rescue provide strong evidence for RGD-dependent regulation. The qPAINT methodology allows single-molecule quantification.

results.result: Activated P2Y2 regulates integrin αV membrane localization in an RGD-dependent manner. ATP stimulation of P2Y2RGD cells increased αV molecules and clusters at the membrane (p=0.0003), also observed in normal AsPC-1 cells (p=0.0382, p=0.0349). P2Y2RGE cells showed more baseline αV (p=0.0003, p=0.0024) but no ATP-induced changes (p=0.7086, p=0.1846). Cluster increase was due to increased total αV proteins (p>0.9999).
results.evaluation: Claims C86-C91 are supported by DNA-PAINT quantification (Figure 4G-H, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C-E). The reciprocal relationship between P2Y2 and αV localization is demonstrated through multiple conditions. The normalization analysis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E) clarifies that clustering reflects total protein increase rather than altered clustering propensity.

results.result: P2Y2 and αV integrins show reciprocal nanoscale interactions. Nearest neighbor distance analysis showed ATP-stimulated P2Y2RGD cells had 103% more αV proteins <50 nm from P2Y2 (p=0.0143), while P2Y2RGE cells showed 43% decrease (p=0.0101). Similar patterns at 20-100 nm range. P2Y2RGD molecules were closer to each other than P2Y2RGE (p<0.0001, p=0.007). This demonstrates reciprocal regulation of membrane localization.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C97 are supported by NND analysis (Figure 4I-L, Figure 4—figure supplement 2). The distance thresholds are justified based on protein dimensions (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A) and validated against randomized controls (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B). The reciprocal interaction is demonstrated through multiple distance ranges and conditions.

results.result: P2Y2-integrin interactions are required for downstream signaling leading to invasion. AsPC-1 cells showed increased FAK and ERK phosphorylation after 15 min ATP stimulation, abrogated by AR-C. Impairing RGD function with cRGDfV or P2Y2RGE mutation decreased p-FAK and p-ERK levels. Targeting the RGD motif impairs receptor signaling and inhibits invasion.
results.evaluation: Claims C98-C100 are supported by western blot analysis (Figure 5A-C) showing time-course phosphorylation of FAK and ERK. The pharmacological (AR-C, cRGDfV) and genetic (P2Y2RGE) approaches converge on the same conclusion. The signaling data mechanistically links the P2Y2-integrin interaction to the invasion phenotype observed in earlier experiments.

results.result: P2Y2 has established roles in hypoxia response, metabolism, and invasion across cancers. Purinergic signaling is classically associated with hypoxia and immune function. P2Y2 has been linked to growth, glycolysis, and HIF-1α expression in PDAC, with AR-C+gemcitabine combination showing efficacy in xenografts. P2Y2 has been implicated in invasion in prostate, breast, and ovarian cancers, with RGD-integrin binding required for tubule formation in 3D models.
results.evaluation: Claims C101-C102, C107-C115 are supported by multiple citations to prior literature (Di Virgilio et al. 2018, Forrester and Williams 1977, Bruns et al. 1986, Feoktistov et al. 2004, Tak et al. 2016, Kwon et al. 2019, Hu et al. 2019, Ko et al. 2012, Wang et al. 2020, Park et al. 2020, Jin et al. 2014, Li et al. 2015, Martínez-Ramírez et al. 2016, Ibuka et al. 2015). These establish the broader context for the current findings.

results.result: P2Y2-integrin interactions represent an alternative therapeutic strategy. No clinically efficacious P2Y2 antagonists exist due to poor bioavailability and selectivity. The current findings demonstrate P2Y2 can be targeted by blocking integrin interactions. GPCR-integrin crosstalk is involved in many processes, but only one prior study examined spatial distribution using conventional IF, lacking nanoscale resolution.
results.evaluation: Claims C116-C122 are supported by citations (Neumann et al. 2022, Wang et al. 2005, Teoh et al. 2012, Erb et al. 2001, Tulapurkar et al. 2005, Chorna et al. 2007). The therapeutic rationale is logical given the experimental findings. The novelty claim regarding super-resolution imaging is supported by the literature review.

results.result: A speculative model proposes that reducing integrin-P2Y2 RGD binding decreases RGD-triggered integrin endocytosis, reducing recycling and increasing surface integrins. This could occur through receptor internalization, RGE mutation, or cRGDfV treatment.
results.evaluation: Claim C123 is explicitly speculative ('We speculate that...') and represents a mechanistic interpretation of the observed data. While the observations (increased surface αV with reduced P2Y2-integrin binding) are supported, the proposed mechanism of altered integrin recycling is not directly tested. Additional experiments tracking integrin endocytosis and recycling would be needed to validate this model.

results.result: This study provides the first single-molecule super-resolution analysis of GPCR-integrin dynamics and demonstrates P2Y2-integrin interactions are required for cancer invasion. P2Y2, via its RGD motif, regulates αV integrin membrane localization to drive ATP-induced PDAC invasion, representing a promising therapeutic target.
results.evaluation: Claims C124-C127 represent the main conclusions of the study. C124 (novelty of super-resolution approach) is supported by literature review. C125 (requirement for invasion) is strongly supported by the genetic, pharmacological, and imaging data. C126 (mechanistic summary) integrates all major findings. C127 (therapeutic potential) is a reasonable inference from the data, though actual therapeutic validation would require additional studies. The claims are well-supported by the comprehensive experimental evidence presented.
